title: An effective Cartier divisor is the zero scheme of a section of its line bundle
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] (a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf which, on the members of some open cover of $X$, is generated by a single nonzerodivisor of the ring of sections), i.e. the ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_D$ of the effective Cartier divisor $D=V(\mathcal I)\subseteq X$. Let $\mathcal O_X(D)=\mathcal I^\vee=\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal I,\mathcal O_X)$ be the associated invertible module [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Then there is a global section $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X(D))$ whose zero scheme $Z(s)$ [def-pc-zero-scheme] is $D$, i.e. whose ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_{Z(s)}$ equals $\mathcal I$. (One such section is the canonical section $1_D$, the global section of $\mathcal{H}om_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal I,\mathcal O_X)$ given by the inclusion $\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_X$.)
